MRK.rationale: Merck's Q1 2026 results reveal a severe fundamental deterioration: a GAAP net loss of $4.24B (EPS -$1.72) driven by a $9B one-time Cidara charge and a $5.8B Terns acquisition-related R&D hit, which together wiped out profitability. While the company claims these are one-time, the operating income swing from +$5.9B (Q1 2025) to -$3.53B (Q1 2026) is dramatic. Revenue grew only 4.9% YoY to $16.29B, and Keytruda concentration remains extreme at ~49% of revenue, creating massive patent cliff risk (2028 expiry). The stock has surged 47% from its October 2025 low of $77.53 to $129.79, yet the P/E has ballooned to 35.9x (vs. 11-14x range in mid-2025) on depressed earnings, and P/B has expanded to 7.0x (vs. 4.0-4.7x range). This is a classic case of price momentum disconnected from deteriorating fundamentals. The market is paying nearly 3x the historical P/E for a company that just posted a massive loss, with Gardasil declining 22% and a failed LITESPARK-012 readout. The LIPFENDRA FDA approval (oral PCSK9 inhibitor) is a modest positive but cannot offset the structural headwinds. Near-term, the October 29 earnings date could catalyze a re-rating downward as the market digests the true cost of the Cidara and Terns deals and the ongoing Keytruda concentration risk.
